newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CUBS TIE MODERN NL RECORD FOR LOSSES AT START OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CUBS TIE MODERN NL RECORD FOR LOSSES AT START OF SEASON.

text.p: The Chicago Cubs tied the modern National League record for losses to start a season when they fell to the Atlanta Braves 6-4 Sunday.

Michael Tucker drove in three runs for the Braves, including a tie-breaking two-run triple in the eighth inning off Turk Wendell (0-1), as the Cubs dropped to 0-10 and tied the NL record set by the Braves in 1988.
The all-time league mark of 0-11 was set by the Detroit Wolverines in 1884. The major league record of 0-21 was set by the Baltimore Orioles in 1988.
The Braves and Florida Marlins are the only teams the Cubs have faced this season.

"We have faced good teams, and we have faced good teams playing good," said Chicago manager Jim Riggleman. "Both teams that we have played against have hit good and pitched good and it doesn't get any easier.
"It's supposed to be tough in the big leagues. You can't ignore what your record is when it's this poor. I don't have a lack of confidence about anybody in the room."
Jeff Blauser and Chipper Jones added sacrifice flies for Atlanta (8-3), which has won eight of its last nine games after starting the season 0-2.
Brad Clontz (2-0), the second of five Atlanta hurlers, was the winner. Mark Wohlers worked the ninth for his fifth save.

In Cincinnati, Pokey Reese started again for the injured Barry Larkin and hit a three-run homer and Dave Burba (2-1) and two relievers combined on a three-hitter to lead the Reds to a 6-4 victory over the Florida Marlins.
The loss was the second in a row after a five-game winning streak and only the third in 11 games for the Marlins.
Reese, a highly-regarded shortstop who is stuck behind Larkin, was recalled from the minors and had the game-winning single in the 10th inning of the Reds' 2-1 victory over the Marlins Saturday.
He blasted his first major league home run off Al Leiter (2-1) in a four-run fourth inning to give the Reds a 5-1 lead. Larkin is bothered by a right heel injury.
In Colorado, Carlos Perez cooled off the hot bats of the Rockies and homered himself as the Montreal Expos snapped a five-game losing streak with an 8-3 victory.

Perez (2-0) allowed three runs -- one earned -- and five hits in 5 1/3 innings. He walked four and struck out none but shut down Colorado, which had scored 71 runs during its seven-game winning streak. The left-hander has looked strong after missing all of 1996 following arm surgery.
Perez connected in the fifth inning off Rockies starter Kevin Ritz (1-2) for his second major-league homer.
In New York, the San Francisco Giants swept a doubleheader from the Mets, 5-1 and 7-6.
Ex-Met Jeff Kent homered, doubled and drove in three runs before leaving the game in the fifth inning with a neck injury as the Giants spoiled New York's home opener.

Kent, playing at Shea Stadium for the first time against his former teammates, hit a two-run homer in a three-run first inning and added an RBI double in the fifth off the Mets' Mark Clark (0-1) to help stake the Giants to a 5-0 lead.

Kent suffered what initially appeared to be a serious injury when he slid head first into third base attempting to stretch a double into a triple on his RBI hit. Kent jolted the neck as he slid and hit his head on the base as he was being tagged by Mets third baseman Edgardo Alfonzo.

He remained on the field for about 10 minutes as both team trainers attended to him and was carried off the field on a stretcher. But X-rays were negative and Kent was diagnosed with a mild neck strain. He is listed as day-to-day.
In the second game, Mark Lewis went 3-for-3 with two solo homers and scored four runs in his first game of the season and Rick Wilkins added three hits and two RBI.
Lewis was playing his first game of the season and first with the Giants after undergoing elbow surgery.
In Philadelphia, Ken Caminiti's RBI double broke a ninth-inning tie and the San Diego Padres capitalised on the control problems of Ricky Bottalico to beeat the Phillies 3-1.

Bottalico (0-1) started the ninth and promptly walked Steve Finley on four pitches. The reliever then went to 2-0 on Caminiti before the reigning National League Most Valuable Player drilled a run-scoring double to right-centre.
Wally Joyner lined out and Greg Vaughn walked before John Flaherty drove in his second run of the game with a single that scored Caminiti.
The rally made a winner of Tim Scott (1-0), who pitched a scoreless eighth.
In Pittsburgh, Todd Hollandsworth had an RBI single and a three-run homer in a nine-run third inning as the Los Angeles Dodgers pounded the Pirates 14-5.
Eric Karros had four hits and three RBI for the Dodgers, who collected 18 hits off seven pitchers and beat the Pirates for the fourth time in five games this season.
In St. Louis, Alan Benes allowed two hits over seven scoreless innings and Gary Gaetti homered and drove in two runs, leading the Cardinals past the Houston Astros 6-2.
Benes (1-1) walked one and struck out nine. Dennis Eckersley recorded the final two outs for his second save.
Mike Hampton (1-2) was reached for four runs and six hits in five innings.
